ce_bugs.text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — embed_category` is deleted unconditionally, but rows are only inserted when `embeddable_hosts` was non-blank; a site that used feed polling (`Jobs::PollFeed` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `import`) with an `embed_category` but no `embeddable_hosts` loses its category mapping entirely and silently begins filing every imported topic under a nil category, because `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category solely from a matching `embeddable_hosts` row.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The TLD pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects `.technology`/`.software`-class TLDs, punycode labels containing digits (`xn--p1ai`), `localhost`, and bare IPs, so those sites cannot be added through the UI; worse, the migration bypasses validation entirely, so such rows can exist in the DB and then fail to save the moment an admin edits them.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The INSERT is built by string interpolation of an admin-controlled site-setting value, so a single quote anywhere in the old `embeddable_hosts` setting aborts the migration mid-deploy (after the table was already created with `force: true`) and is a straightforward SQL injection sink.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` ignores the request body completely and re-renders the current state with 200 OK — a PUT that reports success while persisting nothing; `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls it via `embedding.update({})` yet no template wires a button to that action, so the endpoint ships as a dead, silently-lying write API.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — category: eh.try(:category_id)` is nil whenever the imported URL's host has no `embeddable_hosts` row (notably RSS/feed-polling imports, which are not host-gated), so those topics now land in uncategorized where `SiteSetting.embed_category` used to apply globally

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The host value is string-interpolated straight into SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no quoting: a single apostrophe in the stored setting text breaks the statement and aborts the migration, and since the value is admin-supplied free text this is SQL injection executing as the database owner — use `quote(h)`/a bind parameter.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil and `destroy` (and `update` -> `save_host` at line 10) immediately calls methods on it, so a stale/duplicate delete or any bad id yields a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404; combined with the un-caught client promise the admin sees nothing happen.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`, unlike `save()` right above it, so a failed DELETE (e.g. the 500 from the nil host above) becomes an unhandled rejection: the row stays in the table and the admin gets no error feedback at all.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The only test asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`, a tautology guaranteed by the class definition line, so create/update/destroy, params handling and authz are wholly untested; it passes even though `update`/`destroy` call `nil.host=`/`nil.destroy` for an unknown or already-deleted id (500) and `create` with a blank host hits `self.host.sub!` on nil in EmbeddableHost's before_validation (500 instead of a validation error).
